BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) The legislature intends to rewardschools and school districts with greater autonomy, flexibility, andcontrol over the operation of the schools and districts when recognizedby the state board of education as having exemplary studentperformance, while maintaining the school district's governanceauthority and control of recognized schools by the school districtboard of directors. The legislature finds that increasing flexibilityrequires that only minimal statelevel requirements be imposed upon therecognized schools and districts. It is the intent of the legislaturethat this reward will be an incentive to educators, schools, school SSB 6620 p. 2 districts, and communities to continue to strive towards improvingstudent academic performance through the use of successful learningstrategies. (2) The legislature finds that Washington has a strong history oflocal control and that a locally elected school board is vested withsignificant governance authority over the schools in the district. Thelegislature has no intent to interfere with or lessen that authoritywith this act. Instead, the legislature intends to recognize andreward those school boards of directors that have continually made gooddecisions and have helped to promote successful, productive learningenvironments in the schools by giving the districts even greaterflexibility.

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 28A.305.225 and 2009 c 548 s 503 are each amended toread as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) The state board of education shall continue to refine thedevelopment of an accountability framework that creates a unifiedsystem of support for challenged schools((,)) that aligns with basiceducation, increases the level of support based upon the magnitude ofneed, and uses data for decisions. (2)(a) The state board of education shall develop an accountabilityindex to identify public schools and districts for recognition and foradditional state support. The index shall be based on criteria thatare fair, consistent, and transparent. Performance shall be measuredusing multiple outcomes and indicators including, but not limited to,graduation rates and results from statewide assessments. The indexshall be developed in such a way as to be easily understood by bothemployees within the schools and districts, as well as parents andcommunity members. It is the legislature's intent that the indexprovide feedback to schools and districts to selfassess theirprogress, and enable the identification of schools with exemplary((student)) performance and those that need assistance to overcomechallenges in order to achieve exemplary ((student)) performance. (b) Once the state board of education uses the accountability index((has identified)) to identify schools and school districts for aspecific exemplary performance award, as defined by the state board ofeducation, then the recognized schools or school districts shall berewarded with greater autonomy, flexibility, and control and shall be p. 3 SSB 6620required to meet only the minimal statelevel requirements for twoschool years following the school year in which the school or districtwas recognized; however the school district in which any school isrecognized shall retain governance authority and control of recognizedschools by the school district board of directors. The recognizedschool districts shall retain all the powers and authority of a schooldistrict. The recognized schools and school districts shall complyonly with the following statelevel requirements: (i) To hire, manage, and discharge any school employee inaccordance with the terms of the relevant state law and rules and thelocal collective bargaining agreement, including chapters 41.56, 41.58,and 41.59 RCW; and including employing certificated instructional staffas required in RCW 28A.410.250, but may hire noncertificatedinstructional staff of unusual competence and in exceptional cases asspecified in RCW 28A.150.260; (ii) To comply with the employee record check requirements in RCW28A.400.303; (iii) To adhere to the state and federal health, safety, parents'and students' rights, civil rights, special education, privacy, andnondiscrimination laws, rules, and regulations; (iv) To participate in free and reduced priced meal programs to theextent required by law; (v) To provide the program of basic education required under RCW28A.150.200 as it applies to schools and school districts, andadminister the required statewide assessments under chapter 28A.655 RCWto assess whether a student has met the state standards; (vi) To meet the terms of the performance goals and reportingrequirements under RCW 28A.655.100 and 28A.655.110; (vii) Be subject to the state and federal student accountabilityrequirements; (viii) Be subject to the annual adoption and filing of the districtbudget and financial statements; (ix) Be subject to financial examinations and audits as determinedby the state auditor and the office of the superintendent of publicinstruction, including audits for legal and fiscal compliance; (x) To comply with the requirements of chapter 28A.500 RCW forlocal effort assistance; SSB 6620 p. 4 (xi) To follow the requirements for the election of school districtdirectors as provided in chapter 28A.343 RCW; (xii) To comply with the open public meetings act in chapter 42.30RCW and the open public records requirements in chapter 42.56 RCW; and (xiii) To adhere to the provisions of the interstate compact oneducational opportunity for military children. (b) Once the state board of education uses the accountability indexto identify the schools and districts that need additional help, a morethorough analysis will be done to analyze specific conditions in thedistrict including but not limited to the level of state resources aschool or school district receives in support of the basic educationsystem, achievement gaps for different groups of students, andcommunity support. (3) Based on the accountability index and in consultation with thesuperintendent of public instruction, the state board of educationshall develop a proposal and timeline for implementation of acomprehensive system of voluntary support and assistance for schoolsand districts. The timeline must take into account and accommodatecapacity limitations of the K12 educational system. Changes that havea fiscal impact on school districts, as identified by a fiscal analysisprepared by the office of the superintendent of public instruction,shall take effect only if formally authorized by the legislaturethrough the omnibus appropriations act or other enacted legislation. (4)(a) The state board of education shall develop a proposal andimplementation timeline for a more formalized comprehensive systemimprovement targeted to challenged schools and districts that have notdemonstrated sufficient improvement through the voluntary system. Thetimeline must take into account and accommodate capacity limitations ofthe K12 educational system. The proposal and timeline shall besubmitted to the education committees of the legislature by December 1,2009, and shall include recommended legislation and recommendedresources to implement the system according to the timeline developed. (b) The proposal shall outline a process for addressing performancechallenges that will include the following features: (i) An academicperformance audit using peer review teams of educators that considersschool and community factors in addition to other factors in developingrecommended specific corrective actions that should be undertaken toimprove student learning; (ii) a requirement for the local school board p. 5 SSB 6620plan to develop and be responsible for implementation of correctiveaction plan taking into account the audit findings, which plan must beapproved by the state board of education at which time the plan becomesbinding upon the school district to implement; and (iii) monitoring oflocal district progress by the office of the superintendent of publicinstruction. The proposal shall take effect only if formallyauthorized by the legislature through the omnibus appropriations act orother enacted legislation. (5) In coordination with the superintendent of public instruction,the state board of education shall seek approval from the United Statesdepartment of education for use of the accountability index and thestate system of support, assistance, and intervention, to replace thefederal accountability system under P.L. 107110, the no child leftbehind act of 2001. (6) The state board of education shall work with the education datacenter established within the office of financial management and thetechnical working group established in section 112, chapter 548, Lawsof 2009 to determine the feasibility of using the prototypical fundingallocation model as not only a tool for allocating resources to schoolsand districts but also as a tool for schools and districts to report tothe state legislature and the state board of education on how the stateresources received are being used.

If any part of this act is found to be inconflict with federal requirements that are a prescribed condition tothe allocation of federal funds to the state, the conflicting part ofthis act is inoperative solely to the extent of the conflict and withrespect to the agencies directly affected, and this finding does notaffect the operation of the remainder of this act in its application tothe agencies concerned. Rules adopted under this act must meet federalrequirements that are a necessary condition to the receipt of federalfunds by the state.

If any provision of this act or itsapplication to any person or circumstance is held invalid, theremainder of the act or the application of the provision to other SSB 6620 p. 22 persons or circumstances is not affected.
